assertion_quality.summary: the CTX/CHG set is mostly real: 14 of 15 mutations die on named ids, the two traps the card says it fixed (stale-revision CAS isolation, author-cannot-accept) are genuinely isolated now, and the impact-link assertions are correctly scoped to links whose from_ref is this task. I still found one green assertion that cannot fail for its stated reason, one assertion that is satisfied by the wrong layer, one presence-only assertion whose content the card's own deliverable depends on, and one declared skip whose reason the code contradicts.
assertion_quality.CHG-PLANNER-CANNOT-ACCEPT-ANOTHER-PRINCI: SATISFIED BY THE WRONG LAYER, and the twin of a trap this card already fixed. The frozen contract gives POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/acceptances x-required-roles ['VERIFIER'] (spec/v2.0/contracts/openapi.json), and internal/domain/http.go:120-128 refuses any principal without that role with 403 'role not authorized for operation' before acceptChange is ever reached. The principal used here (w0402-planner) holds OWNER, PLANNER, EXECUTOR, SCHEDULER and no VERIFIER, so the id is green on the role gate, not on independence. It also accepts 'code == 403 || code == 409' - two different rules - and never inspects the message, unlike its sibling CHG-AUTHOR-CANNOT-ACCEPT-OWN-CHANGE which does check 'author cannot independently accept'. No mutation covers it. Either give the refus-er the VERIFIER role and assert the specific independence message, or restate the id as what it actually tests (role gating, which is the API contract's property, not this card's).
assertion_quality.CTX-TAMPERED-BUNDLE-REFUSED: cannot distinguish the layer it names. The if/else passes on BOTH outcomes (storage refused the write, or the service refused the read), so today it is green because of the store; the sibling id CTX-CONTEXT-READABLE-AGAIN-AFTER-RESTORE that would have exercised the service branch is unreachable in practice and does not appear in the 239 emitted ids at all. My forge probe shows the service check does work when reached. Honest disclosure exists (Z3 survivor), but the id name overstates what the green id evidences: split it into two ids, or keep the accept-both shape and rename it to say 'a stored bundle cannot be silently altered at either layer'.
assertion_quality.CTX-BUNDLE-CARRIES-ALL-REQUIRED-FIELDS: the 17-field list is genuinely the frozen schema list - it matches spec/v2.0/contracts/domain.schema.json ContextBundle.required exactly, so the 'read from the schema, not from what the implementation emits' comment is true. But presence is all it checks: unresolved_items and unfinished_commitments pass as empty arrays. Combined with VE4 below, presence-with-wrong-content is exactly the failure mode this card is exposed to.
assertion_quality.CTX-MATERIALIZE-MANIFEST-NAMES-BUNDLE-AN: name promises more than it verifies, and the '||' fallback weakens it: it passes if the bundle id merely appears anywhere in the manifest bytes. materialize.go:187 writes an explicit 'resume_instruction' and a 'bundle_ref'; neither is read by any id. Nothing in the 239 asserts the recovered next step at all (no id reads next_task_id, unfinished_commitments or resume_instruction), so the deliverable sentence 'a new session or worker recovers the accurate next step' is currently evidenced by carriage, not by accuracy.
assertion_quality.CTX-STALE-CAS-ISOLATED-FROM-PRECONDITION: a control assertion (current revision != 99999) rather than a property; near-zero falsifiability but legitimate as the paired witness for the CAS isolation fix. Flagging only so the count is not read as 239 properties.
assertion_quality.CTX-MATERIALIZE-ENTRIES-RESOLVE-UNDER-WO: the filepath.IsAbs(full) conjunct is vacuous because the workspace is absolute; the real teeth are the '..' prefix test, which is sound. Note also that every delivered entry name is service-minted, so the escape test is currently a guard against a shape the service itself does not produce; my VC3 probe confirms the request schema does not let a client supply an id, so the name source is not attacker-controlled today.
assertion_quality.assertions_without_teeth_admitted_by_the: CHG-CONFLICT-DOES-NOT-OVERWRITE-A-DRAFT is disclosed as recording behaviour rather than proving a guard; I agree with that disclosure and add that CHG-RESOLUTION-KEEPS-BOTH-DRAFTS has the same property, so two of the conflict ids are observational.

can_a_worker_be_handed_a_manifest_whose_.detail: the delivered ids re-hash every entry from disk (my run: named>0 and hashed==named). My own probe then chmod-ed a delivered input, rewrote it, and confirmed the manifest hash no longer matches, so a worker can detect it; a second worker still receives the sealed bytes because MaterializeTaskContext reads uploaded_content, not the previous workspace. But no operation re-verifies a workspace once handed over, and the private-memory half of the negative ('private memory overriding project truth') is not asserted anywhere in the 239 - it is only implied by the delivered inputs being read-only (CTX-MATERIALIZE-INPUT-IS-THE-SEALED-BYTES-READ-ONLY, killed by Z6).
can_a_worker_be_handed_a_manifest_whose_.not_fully_covered: '未注入文件却自报读取' (a worker claiming to have read a file it was never given) is covered structurally - the workspace is created empty and every entry must be manifest-named and hash-matched - but there is no assertion that a file the worker was NOT given cannot be reached: the destination argument is not confined to any authorised root (materialize.go:151 only absolutises it), so a caller with a valid grant can materialize the project's context anywhere on the filesystem. That is a host-boundary question for W04-01/W08 rather than a step-2 failure, and I flag it as an observation, not a block.

resolveConflict_fix_is_too_broad.detail: a conflict over two drafts on ProjectState.current_decision_refs was flipped to RESOLVED, with resolution_proposal_id set, by an APPLIED change whose only edit was a Requirement's text field. Blast radius is limited: the conflicted draft still cannot be accepted afterwards (409 'edited value changed since proposal'), so this is record integrity rather than an authority bypass.
resolveConflict_fix_is_too_broad.what_a_real_guard_would_check: that the settling change touches the conflict's subject_refs or its blocked scope, which is what applyChange already does through proposal.conflict_ids; resolveConflict should require the same relation, or refuse a change that shares no edit target with the conflict's subjects.

scope_question.does_the_context.go_decision_merge_over_: no. It reads only ProjectState.current_decision_refs and each decision's own supersedes_id, adds them to the freeze's latest_decision_refs and continuation block, and neither creates lineage rows nor mutates the decision_lineage table that revalidateTask owns. It is the minimal way to satisfy '有效/废弃决定' for a task that names no inputs, and my own fresh-session probe shows it doing that job. Defect (b) as described is real and the fix is in the right place.
scope_question.the_one_overstatement_in_the_fix: the comment and the checkpoint claim that a decision which 'no longer resolves' is reported through unresolved_items rather than failing the freeze. Only the object-missing branch degrades; a ref whose pinned version row is missing or whose content hash differs still aborts the whole freeze at context.go:375 (version -> 422 GATE_FAILED / CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH). And the degraded branch is unreachable through the API, because validateDecisions already requires version() for every ref entering current_decision_refs (changes.go:82-118). So the claim describes a behaviour nothing exercises and partly contradicts.

notes_for_the_executor: Your implementation is good and I want to be clear about that: both fixes are real (I reverted both files and the check dies on exactly the five ids that should die), the mutation set is honest, the Z3 disclosure checks out under an attack I designed myself, and the fresh-session decision recovery works when I test it outside your assertions. The reject is about what the evidence says, not what the code does.

For item 1, the cheapest honest version: after applyChange on the Requirement, read the stored proposal and assert impacted_refs and impact_link_ids are exactly the closure the freeze wrote, plus a mutation that blanks them at creation. Do not re-declare this as W06 territory.

For item 2, look at how you fixed AA1: same principal set, different subject. Then make the mutation 'acceptance by a non-author verifier still works' and 'acceptance by the author fails' both land, so the id cannot be satisfied by the role gate again.

For items 3 and 4, note they are the same knot: applyChange already resolves the proposal's own conflict_ids AND prunes state.blocking_conflict_ids, while resolveConflict does neither. The narrow fix is to have resolveConflict require a relation to the conflict's subjects and prune the id, and then assert that a later freeze reports no phantom unresolved_items. That single change closes both.

Item 5 wants one assertion pair, not a new architecture: freeze -> deliver -> read manifest.json and assert the next step the bundle names is the unfinished task the state still holds, and add a failure (a blocked requirement or a recorded NoProgress) that must survive the freeze.

Please make the note self-verifying: pin the sha256 of the check report and of each mutation file inside the note, generate the provenance list after the copies rather than before, and let the generator take the product-defect list as data so it cannot log the same event three times.

When you re-present, a reviewer should be able to check the numbers from the note alone. Right now three of them (39 vs 41 CHG, 14/15 vs 13/14, six failing legacy tests) only reconcile by going into git history, which is how this family got rejected before.

The flake I hit (TestRuntimeCoordinatorConcurrentSealConflict, 1 of 2 attempts in the broad selection, 0 of 3 in isolation) is not yours, but record per-attempt outcomes in the note so the next reviewer does not have to decide whether you hid something. Another window was dispatching test.context during my review, so serialise evidence runs explicitly.
